frontMatter.welcome:
At Novopor Advanced Science Pvt. Ltd., innovation fuels our mission — but safety is its backbone. Whether you’re working in a lab, handling advanced materials, or managing logistics, your well-being is our top priority. Health and safety at Novopor are not a rulebook; it’s a culture we build together.

- Right to Participate – Through safety committees and joint health initiatives.

Novopor has evolved into a leading player in the Indian and international markets for high-performance chemicals. With manufacturing units and a state-of-the-art Innovation Centre, we collaborate with global partners to create customized, sustainable, and performance-driven solutions.
Our work spans three core areas:
- Agrochemicals – empowering modern agriculture with effective, environmentally conscious solutions.
- Material Science – developing specialized materials that meet today’s industrial and environmental standards.
- Performance Chemicals – offering advanced formulations that enhance performance in a range of sectors, from construction to consumer goods.
At Novopor, our purpose is clear and unwavering:
To advance the quality of life by developing innovative, efficient, and sustainable chemical solutions that meet the demands of a changing world.
We hold ourselves accountable to the highest standards of:
- Scientific Excellence – developing with precision, testing with integrity.
- Sustainability & Responsibility – minimizing our footprint and maximizing long-term impact.
- People Empowerment – investing in the people who drive our innovation forward.
The Employee Handbook is applicable to all employees, contractors, sub-contractors, and all internal and external stakeholders of Stella Hospitality. It applies to all our locations.

frontMatter.purpose: At Novopor Advanced Science Pvt. Ltd., we believe operational excellence goes hand-in-hand with employee well-being. chapters.title: Working Hours & Attendance Management
chapters.text:
## Standard Working Hours:
[table]
| Shift | HO | R & D | Unit 5 | Unit 6 |
| General Shift | 09:00 – 18:00 | 09:00 – 17:30 |
| 1st Shift | - | 07:00 – 14:00 | 06:00 – 14:00 |
| 2nd Shift | - | 14:00 – 22:00 |
| 3rd Shift | - | 22:00 – 07:00 | 22:00 – 06:00 |
- Employees must arrive on time, and regular attendance is crucial for productivity. ​
- Breaks are mandated, with a minimum of a half-hour rest after five hours of work. ​
- Overtime is compensated at twice the ordinary wage rate for hours exceeding nine in a day or 48 in a week. ​
- Disciplinary actions may be taken for consistent tardiness or absences without proper notification.
## Attendance Management and Biometric System
- All full-time employees, contractual staff, and on-site vendors must use biometric terminals located at facility entrances.
- Employees must scan their fingerprint upon arrival and departure to log their work hours.
- The system integrates with the HR LMS portal, updating attendance records in real-time.
Data Security
- Biometric data is encrypted and stored securely in compliance with data protection regulations.
- Access to attendance records is restricted to HR personnel and authorized managers.
- Employees can view their attendance logs via the HR LMS portal for transparency.
- In case of system errors (e.g., scanner failure), employees must report to HR immediately and manually log their time, subject to manager verification.
- Regular maintenance of biometric terminals ensures operational reliability.
Attendance Expectations
- Punctuality: Employees must arrive on time for their designated shifts, as regular attendance is critical for productivity.
- Breaks: A minimum half-hour rest break is mandated after five hours of work, tracked via the biometric system for compliance.
Work-from-Home Attendance:
- Employees working from home must register their work hours through the HR LMS portal, with manager approval.
- Work-from-home arrangements may be terminated based on business needs, and managers may request employees to report to the office as required.
- No more than 10% of a team may work from home on any given day, monitored by Line Function Heads.
Disciplinary Actions
Tardiness or Absences:
- Consistent tardiness or unnotified absences may result in disciplinary actions:
- 1st Instance: Verbal warning.
- 2nd Instance: Written warning.
- 3rd Instance: Salary deduction or suspension.
- Unauthorized absences are treated as Leave Without Pay, and continuous absence of 8+ days may lead to termination.
Falsification:
- Tampering with biometric records or falsifying attendance data leads to immediate disciplinary action, including potential termination.
## Flexibility:
Overview: The document outlines NOVOPOR's Flexitime Policy, detailing work-from-home eligibility, conditions, and procedures for employees. ​
## Work Hour Flexibility Program
- Flextime allows employees to choose their work hours for better work-life balance. ​
- Employees can work from home under specific conditions, limited to India. ​
- A maximum of 60 days can be availed annually, accruing at 5 days per month for new employees. ​
## Working from Home Eligibility ​
- Employees must balance work deliverables with personal commitments, including emergencies. ​
- Home working is suitable for jobs that do not impair productivity or compliance. ​
- Employees need sufficient knowledge, responsibility, and self-motivation for independent work. ​
## Technical Requirements
- Employees must have a home broadband connection with a minimum bandwidth of 100 Mbps and 2 Mbps working speed. ​
- Novopor is not responsible for broadband setup, maintenance, or costs associated with home infrastructure. ​
- Employees must use Novopor-issued laptops and adhere to IT security protocols. ​
## Work Time and Registration
- Employees must work within the limits of the Work Time policy. ​
- Registration for working from home is done through the HR LMS portal and requires line manager approval. ​
## Termination of Working from Home ​
- The company can terminate work-from-home arrangements based on business needs.
- Managers can request employees to report to the office as required. ​
## Security and Confidentiality
- Employees must secure company resources and maintain confidentiality. ​
- Confidential information must be disposed of or returned according to guidelines.
- Only Novopor-issued laptops should be used, with necessary security measures in place. ​
## Responsibility of Managers
- Clear objectives and task allocations are essential for successful home working. ​
- Line Function Heads must monitor that no more than 10% of their team works from home on any given day. ​
## Application Procedure
- For ≤5 working days, employees apply via the HR LMS portal; for >5 days, a discussion with the manager is required. ​
- Home working can be prefixed or suffixed with leave but not both. ​
- Exceptions require approval from the CEO and Head of Human Resources.

## Career Progression Framework
## Objective
At Novopor Advanced Sciences Pvt. Ltd., promotions reflect our commitment to recognizing and rewarding consistent high performance, dedication, and leadership potential. This ensures that the process of career progression is fair, transparent, and aligned with the company’s performance management framework and organizational needs.
## Eligibility Criteria
To be considered for promotion, employees must:
- Have completed at least 12 months in their current role.
- Not be under a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) at the time of review.
- Have received a minimum performance rating of ‘B’ or above in the most recent performance appraisal.
- Demonstrate capability to take on additional responsibilities or a higher role.
- Meet any role-specific qualifications or certifications, if applicable.
Employees who have joined after 30th September of the financial year will not be eligible for performance-based promotions in that cycle but will be reviewed in the following year.
Promotion decisions are closely tied to the annual Performance Management System (PMS).
- The PMS cycle follows the financial year (April–March).
- Performance is assessed through structured objective setting, departmental alignment, and annual reviews.
- Employees rated ‘A’ (120%) or ‘B’ (100%) are typically considered for career advancement, depending on available opportunities and business priorities.
## Promotion Process
- Manager Recommendation: The line manager assesses the employee’s readiness for promotion based on performance reviews, skills, and business need.
- HR Review: HR validates eligibility, checks internal equity, and reviews prior ratings and feedback.
- Department Head Approval: Final promotion decisions require department head concurrence and may be routed to top management for critical roles.
- Communication: All confirmed promotions are formally communicated by the HR Department with the effective date.
Promotions are generally considered during the annual appraisal cycle, but off-cycle promotions may be permitted in exceptional circumstances such as new role creation, critical backfills, or significant project success.
## Performance Improvement & Promotion Hold
Employees under a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) are not eligible for promotion during the duration of the plan. Promotions may resume once the employee successfully completes the plan and demonstrates sustained improvement.
## Transparency and Appeals
We believe in open and constructive dialogue. Employees who have queries about promotion decisions can approach the HR department in writing within 15 days of receiving communication. Appeals will be reviewed by HR and the concerned department head for fair and impartial consideration.

chapters.title: Diversity, Equity & Inclusion
chapters.text:
## ntroduction
At Novopor Advanced Sciences Pvt. Ltd., we are committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, and inclusive work environment where all individuals—regardless of background, identity, or ability—are respected, empowered, and given equal opportunities to succeed. We believe that diversity drives innovation, equity ensures fairness, and inclusion strengthens our company culture.
## Our Commitment
We are dedicated to building a workplace rooted in gender equality, social justice, and respect for all intersecting identities. We also recognize sexual and reproductive rights as essential human rights and integrate these principles into our organizational values and ESG strategy.
## Accessibility & Inclusion
## nclusive Workplace Culture:
- Internal Job Postings (IJP) prioritize visibility for underrepresented groups.
- Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) are encouraged to support minority communities.
- Outreach efforts actively engage veterans, persons with disabilities, and marginalized ethnic groups.
- Junior employees from minority backgrounds are supported through structured mentorship.
- Leadership development programs aim to accelerate career growth for underrepresented talent.
## Workplace Accessibility & Accommodations:
- Facilities are designed to be physically accessible.
- Assistive technology is provided where needed.
- Flexible work arrangements are offered for health or personal requirements.
- Employees can confidentially request accommodations through HR.
- Inclusion Task Force reviews workplace policies for fairness and accessibility.
- Regular employee feedback sessions support continuous improvement.
## Employee Resource Groups (ERGs)
We encourage employees to participate in or form ERGs to build community and promote inclusivity:
- Diversity & Inclusion ERG – Offers support and networking for minority groups.
- LGBTQ Inclusion Group – Advocates inclusive policies and awareness.
- Cultural & Ethnic Inclusion Network – Fosters intercultural understanding through events and dialogues.
## Gender Equality Initiatives
- Executive sponsorship programs promote women and gender-diverse leadership.
- Flexible schedules and hybrid work support gender-inclusive work-life balance.
- CSR initiatives focus on girl education and STEM learning.
- We collaborate with NGOs that advocate for gender rights and representation.

## External Stakeholder Human Rights
## ntroduction
At Novopor Advanced Science Pvt. Ltd., we understand that our impact goes beyond our factories, laboratories, and offices. As a responsible corporate citizen, we are committed to upholding human rights not only within our workforce but across our supply chain, business partners, and the communities in which we operate.
Our Human Rights commitments align with the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs), the International Bill of Human Rights, ILO Core Conventions, and OECD Guidelines. We recognize human rights as inherent, indivisible, and universal—applicable to all people, regardless of nationality, gender, ethnicity, or status.
This section outlines our holistic approach to respecting and safeguarding the human rights of all external stakeholders—defined as individuals or groups outside the organization who may be affected by our activities, decisions, and value chain operations.
## External Stakeholders
We engage with a diverse range of external stakeholders, including:
- Customers and consumers
- Suppliers and third-party vendors
- Distributors and contractors
- Community-based organizations and NGOs
- Indigenous groups and impacted communities
- Local authorities, regulators, and investors
We maintain transparent, consistent, and inclusive dialogue with stakeholders to identify and address actual or potential human rights risks proactively.
Particular emphasis is given to traditionally marginalized groups such as women, youth, indigenous peoples, and economically vulnerable populations.
Stakeholder feedback is integrated into decision-making, and we regularly inform them about the impact of their contributions.
## Business Partner Expectations
We require our business partners, suppliers, and contractors to uphold standards of responsible business conduct that reflect our Human Rights Policy.
- Suppliers are assessed through a risk-based due diligence program
- Contracts include human rights clauses aligned with international norms
- Blacklisting of non-compliant vendors is practiced when violations are confirmed
- We prioritize collaboration with suppliers in high-risk sectors to prevent human rights abuse, particularly in resource extraction or conflict zones
## Monitoring & Continuous Improvement
- Conduct annual Human Rights Impact Assessments (HRIAs) in high-risk areas
- Use third-party auditors to verify worker conditions and community impacts
- Maintain a Human Rights Risk Register linked to our ESG dashboard
- Gather anonymous feedback via community surveys and engagement forums
- Offer regular training on rights and grievance channels to suppliers and external reps
- Integrate lessons learned into future policy design and risk prevention
- Consult external human rights experts to ensure alignment with evolving risks and emerging best practices
- Regularly benchmark our performance using global frameworks like the UNGP Reporting Framework
- future policy design and risk prevention

chapters.title: Grievance Mechanism
chapters.text:
## ntroduction
At Novopor Advanced Sciences Pvt. Ltd., we are committed to providing a fair, respectful, and responsive grievance mechanism in line with our dedication to ethical, social, and environmental responsibility. This mechanism ensures that all employees, contract workers, suppliers, and external stakeholders can report concerns or violations confidentially and without retaliation. It aligns with international standards including the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, ILO conventions, and EcoVadis requirements.
Grievances may be raised for, but are not limited to, the following concerns:
- Labor Practices & Working Conditions: Excessive working hours, forced labor, child labor, discrimination, harassment, or unfair wages.
- Health, Safety & Wellbeing: Unsafe work environments, exposure to hazardous substances, denial of protective equipment.
- Ethical Business Conduct: Bribery, corruption, conflict of interest, facilitation payments, or any breach of the Company’s Code of Conduct.
- Human Rights: Violations impacting individuals or communities, including land rights, freedom of association, or abuse in the supply chain.
- Environmental Concerns: Improper waste disposal, air/water pollution, ecosystem damage, and failure to meet environmental compliance.
- Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DE&I): Any exclusionary practices based on gender, caste, ethnicity, religion, disability, or other protected characteristics.
- Supply Chain Violations: Involvement of vendors or subcontractors in unethical practices such as modern slavery, illegal sourcing, or ESG violations.
- Transparency & ESG Reporting: Falsification or concealment of ESG data, impact assessments, or audit results.
## Reporting Channels
To promote accessibility and confidentiality, Novopor provides the following grievance channels:
- 24/7 Ethics Hotline – Toll-free number available in multiple languages
- Online Grievance Form – www.novopor.ethicsportal.com (anonymous reporting enabled)
- Grievance Box – Available at all manufacturing, warehousing, and project locations
- Community Liaison Desk – During stakeholder consultations or public hearings
- Email – humanrights@novopor.in
## Redressal Process
Novopor has established a tiered grievance redressal system to ensure efficient and fair resolution:
## Level 01 – Supervisor Level
- Grievance submitted in writing to the immediate supervisor
- Acknowledgement: within 1 working day
- Resolution Timeline: 2 working days
- If unresolved, escalated to Level 02
## Level 02 – Grievance Officer
- Complaint submitted to designated Grievance Officer
- Acknowledgement: within 1 working day
- Counseling and investigation: within 3 working days
- If unsatisfactory, escalated to Level 03
## Level 03 – Grievance Redressal Committee
- Formal complaint lodged with Grievance Redressal Committee (comprising one Functional Director, one HR representative, and the Company Secretary)
- Deliberation and Recommendation: within 7 working days
- Final Decision by Management: within a maximum of 14 working days
## Remediation & Follow-up
Where grievances are found valid, Novopor undertakes proportionate and fair corrective actions:
[table]
| Remediation Stage | Action |
| Immediate Relief | Cease any ongoing harm and ensure safety of the complainant |
| Support Services | Legal assistance, counseling, or rehabilitation in partnership with NGOs |
| Restitution | Financial or operational compensation, as applicable |
| Disciplinary Action | Suspension or removal of employee/vendor as per Code of Conduct |
| Disclosure | Transparent sharing of grievance outcomes (where permitted by law) |
| Stakeholder Engagement | Rebuilding trust with affected stakeholders through dialogue |
## Monitoring & Continuous Improvement
To maintain and enhance effectiveness, the Company will:
- Conduct Human Rights & Environmental Impact Assessments in high-risk operations
- Perform independent audits to evaluate grievance processes and working conditions
- Update the ESG Risk Register to reflect emerging risks and grievance trends
- Deliver annual training on grievance redressal, ethics, and rights protection
- Encourage anonymous feedback and whistleblower submissions via secure platforms
- Review and improve the mechanism annually in line with EcoVadis best practices
## Reporting
The Grievance Redressal Committee shall submit a annual report to the Management detailing the number, type, and resolution of grievances. These are reviewed for systemic improvements and ethical performance monitoring.
